---
description: "How often Island Transit's buses left on time, day by day and hour by hour, and how the figures are checked."
title: "On time"
subtitle: "The whole system, day by day and hour by hour"
---

::: {.method-note}
We calculate these figures ourselves from Island Transit's bus locations and
schedule, so they aren't official numbers. The feed has no "minutes late"
field, which means our script has to figure out the moment each bus left a
stop from where the bus was just before and just after. Automated checks
compare those times with the feed's own stop reports on every route every
day, and we have also timed buses in person on route 60. The [Methods](methods.qmd) page explains it all, and
[Routes](routes.qmd) shows one route at a time.
:::

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
//| output: false
import {csv, json, pct, num, count, band, lateness, longDate, isoDate, serviceDays, MIN_OBSERVED, SERIES, REPO_URL, DATA_URL, RELEASES_URL} from "./lib.js"
daily = csv(d3, "data/ontime/daily.csv")
// Days with scheduled service; a holiday is archived but not charted.
days = serviceDays(daily).map(d => ({...d, day: isoDate(d.service_date), date: new Date(`${isoDate(d.service_date)}T12:00:00Z`)}))
latestDate = days.length ? days.at(-1).day : null
latest = latestDate ? json(`data/ontime/days/${latestDate}.json`) : null
noData = () => html`<p class="empty">No day has been processed yet.</p>`
// The daily table lists the day but its detail file did not load.
noDetail = () => days.length === 0 ? noData() : html`<p class="empty">The details for ${longDate(latestDate)} can't be shown right now.</p>`
```

## Day by day

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
html`${days.length === 0 ? noData() : days.length < 2
  ? html`<p class="empty">So far there is one day of data, ${longDate(latestDate)}, and ${pct(days[0].on_time_share_of_observed)} of the departures we saw that day were on time.
      A day-by-day trend line will appear once a second day comes in.</p>`
  : Plot.plot({
    ariaLabel: "Share of departures on time, by service day",
    ariaDescription: `From ${longDate(days[0].day)} to ${longDate(latestDate)}. On the latest day, ${pct(days.at(-1).on_time_share_of_observed)} of the departures seen were on time.`,
    style: {background: "transparent"},
    width: Math.max(320, Math.min(width, 960)), height: 240, marginLeft: 50, marginRight: 30,
    x: {type: "utc", label: null, ticks: days.length <= 8 ? days.map(d => d.date) : 8, tickFormat: "%b %-d"},
    y: {grid: true, label: "On time", domain: [0, 1], tickFormat: d => `${Math.round(d * 100)}%`},
    marks: [
      Plot.ruleY([0]),
      Plot.lineY(days, {x: "date", y: "on_time_share_of_observed", stroke: SERIES, strokeWidth: 2}),
      Plot.dot(days, {x: "date", y: "on_time_share_of_observed", fill: SERIES, r: 4}),
      Plot.tip(days, Plot.pointerX({x: "date", y: "on_time_share_of_observed",
        title: d => `${longDate(d.day)}\n${pct(d.on_time_share_of_observed, 1)} on time\n${pct(d.observed_share)} of departures seen`})),
    ],
  })}`
```

## Hour by hour

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
hours = latest == null ? [] : Object.entries(latest.by_hour).map(([h, b]) => ({
  hour: +h, ...b, band: band(b.on_time_share_of_observed, b.observed),
  label: `${(+h % 12) || 12} ${+h < 12 ? "AM" : "PM"}`}))
  .filter(d => d.observed >= MIN_OBSERVED)
html`${hours.length === 0 ? noDetail() : html`<p class="note">This chart shows ${longDate(latestDate)}, grouped by the hour each departure was scheduled, in Pacific time. We leave out any hour in which we saw fewer than ${MIN_OBSERVED} departures.</p>
  ${Plot.plot({
    ariaLabel: `Share of departures on time by scheduled hour, ${longDate(latestDate)}`,
    ariaDescription: hours.map(d => `${d.label}: ${pct(d.on_time_share_of_observed)}`).join(", "),
    style: {background: "transparent"},
    width: Math.max(320, Math.min(width, 960)), height: 240, marginLeft: 50,
    x: {label: null, domain: hours.map(d => d.label), padding: 0.25},
    y: {grid: true, label: "On time", domain: [0, 1], tickFormat: d => `${Math.round(d * 100)}%`},
    marks: [
      Plot.barY(hours, {x: "label", y: "on_time_share_of_observed", fill: d => d.band.color, rx: 3}),
      Plot.ruleY([0]),
      Plot.tip(hours, Plot.pointerX({x: "label", y: "on_time_share_of_observed",
        title: d => `${d.label}\n${pct(d.on_time_share_of_observed)} on time\nTypically ${lateness(d.deviation_s_median)}\n${count(d.observed)} of ${count(d.scheduled)} departures seen`})),
    ],
  })}`}`
```

## How these numbers are checked

<details class="more"><summary>Automatic checks, every route, every day</summary>

Our script runs two automatic checks every day, without anyone needing to go
out and watch the buses ([Methods](methods.qmd), section 5). The first check uses a
clue the feed already gives us. Each bus report names the stop the bus is
heading for, and that name switches to the next stop once the bus passes. If
our departure time lands between the last report naming a stop and the first
report naming a later one, give or take 30 seconds, it agrees with the feed.
The second check looks at the time it took to get from one stop to the next.
That time should never run backwards, and it should never mean the bus went
faster than 126 km/h (about 78 mph).

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
val = latest?.validation ?? null
checks = val == null ? [] : [
  ["Inferred departures compared with the feed", count(val.feed_agreement.compared)],
  ["Agree with the feed's change of stop (within 30 s)", pct(val.feed_agreement.within_tolerance_share, 1)],
  ["Median time from inferred departure to the first report naming the next stop",
    `${num(val.feed_agreement.feed_change_after_departure_s.median, 1)} s`],
  ["Times the feed's stop sequence went backwards within a trip", val.feed_agreement.feed_sequence_going_backwards],
  ["Segments between inferred times", count(val.travel_times.segments)],
  ["Segments running backwards in time", val.travel_times.negative],
  ["Segments faster than 126 km/h (78 mph)", val.travel_times.over_max_speed],
].map(([check, value]) => ({check, value}))
html`${checks.length === 0 ? noDetail() : Inputs.table(checks, {select: false, header: {check: "Check", value: "Result"}, rows: 10})}`
```

</details>

<details class="more"><summary>Timed in person on route 60</summary>

To make sure our times match what really happens on the street, we time
buses in person and compare. The goal is for our times to be off by 30
seconds or less on average. So far we have done this only on route 60,
riding on board, so it doesn't yet cover other routes, buses leaving after they have
waited at a timepoint, or buses leaving a terminal. The two automatic checks
above still cover every route every day. The person timing the bus notes the
same moments our method looks for: when the bus comes within 40 meters
(about 130 feet) of the stop, and when it gets more than 40 meters past it. From on board, it is often
easier to note the moment the bus is level with the stop, and we compare
that with the midpoint of our two times.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
fc = json("data/ontime/field-check.json")
fcRows = fc == null || fc.overall.n === 0 ? [] : [["All", fc.overall], ["Arrivals (130 ft before the stop)", fc.arrival], ["Departures (130 ft past the stop)", fc.departure], ["Level with the stop", fc.pass ?? {n: 0}]]
  .filter(([, s]) => s.n > 0)
  .map(([moment, s]) => ({moment, n: s.n, bias: s.bias_s, mae: s.mae_s, w30: s.within_30s_share, w60: s.within_60s_share}))
html`${fcRows.length === 0
  ? html`<p>No timed observations have been scored yet${fc && fc.rows_waiting_for_their_day ? `, and ${fc.rows_waiting_for_their_day} are waiting for their day to be processed` : ""}.</p>`
  : html`<p>We have scored ${fc.overall.n} timed moments over ${fc.days.length} day${fc.days.length === 1 ? "" : "s"}.
      Each difference is our time minus the timed one, in seconds, so a positive bias means our times run late.
      ${fc.meets_target == null ? `The 30-second target is judged once there are ${fc.target_min_n ?? 5} timed moments.` : fc.meets_target ? "The average difference meets the 30-second target." : "The average difference has not yet met the 30-second target."}</p>
    ${Inputs.table(fcRows, {select: false,
      header: {moment: "", n: "Timed", bias: "Bias (s)", mae: "Mean absolute difference (s)", w30: "Within 30 s", w60: "Within 60 s"},
      format: {bias: d => num(d, 1), mae: d => num(d, 1), w30: d => pct(d), w60: d => pct(d)}, rows: 5})}`}`
```
